en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cones in the world.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 900 square kilometers.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine eagle, found in the forests of Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles globally.
The waling-waling orchid, native to Mindanao, is highly prized by collectors for its beautiful and colorful cascading flower clusters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral ecosystems.
The Philippines experiences the amihan, a cool northeast monsoon, from November to February, bringing dry weather to most regions.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest reserves of nickel, which is heavily mined in provinces like Surigao.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural landscapes carved into the mountains over two thousand years ago.
